definitions.gloss: to obligate; to make mandatory; to require by rule or law
definitions.explanation: To impose an obligation or requirement, typically through law, regulation, or organizational rules. Often used in passive form to describe what is required.

examples.japanese: {届|とど}け{出|で}が{義務付|ぎむづ}けられている。
{法律|ほうりつ}で{報告|ほうこく}を{義務付|ぎむづ}ける。
{企業|きぎょう}に{情報|じょうほう}{公開|こうかい}が{義務付|ぎむづ}けられるようになった。
examples.english: Companies became required to disclose information.

notes:
An ichidan verb formed from {義務|ぎむ} (obligation, duty) + {付|づ}ける (to attach). Creates the meaning of attaching an obligation to something or someone. Very frequently used in passive form ({義務付|ぎむづ}けられている) to describe existing requirements.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive — takes を to mark the action being made mandatory, and に to mark who is obligated.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {義務付|ぎむづ}けられている — is required, is mandatory
- {法律|ほうりつ}で{義務付|ぎむづ}ける — to require by law
- {義務付|ぎむづ}けられた{研修|けんしゅう} — mandatory training

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {義務化|ぎむか}する — to make obligatory (noun + する form)
- {強制|きょうせい}する — to compel, to force (stronger, more coercive)
- {課|か}す — to impose (a duty, tax, etc.)
